output:
I checked the catalog entries I have in memory and found these relevant items: “adjustable desk lamps,” “desk lamp,” “task lamps,” “lighting products,” and a named model “Harbor Task Lamp.” The catalog items show there are suitable LED task/adjustable lamps available, and one specific model listed by name — but the memory does not include technical specs for any lamp.

Recommendation summary (what to consider)
- Preferred type: an LED adjustable task/desk lamp with good glare control and a dimmer. These give the best energy efficiency and useful control for office work.
- Key performance targets to look for on the product spec sheet:
  - Light output: ~400–800 lumens (typical desk-task range).
  - Power: roughly 5–15 W (LED) for the lumen range above — look at lumens per watt (efficacy). Aim for ≥80 lm/W for an efficient lamp.
  - Color temperature: 3500–4000 K for neutral/comfortable office lighting (cooler if you prefer a bright “focus” feel).
  - Color rendering (CRI): ≥90 for the best color accuracy; CRI ≥80 is acceptable for many offices.
  - Dimming: smooth dimming to at least 10% is useful for task control and extra energy savings.
  - Controls/features that save energy: automatic shutoff/occupancy sensor or motion sensor, programmable timers, or smart (app/schedule) control.
  - Certifications: ENERGY STAR or DLC listed are helpful indicators for verified efficiency and may qualify for rebates.
  - Lifetime and warranty: long rated lifetime (25,000–50,000 hours) and a multi-year warranty reduce lifecycle cost.

Why those specs
- Lumens and lux determine how bright the workspace will be; 300–500 lux is a common target for desk work, which typically maps to the lumen range above depending on fixture and desk size.
- Efficacy (lm/W) and wattage directly determine energy consumption. Higher lm/W = fewer watts to get the same light.
- CRI and color temperature affect visual comfort and color accuracy for tasks like reading, paperwork, screens.
- Dimming and smart/occupancy controls reduce run-time and therefore energy use.
- ENERGY STAR/DLC provide third‑party verification that the product meets efficiency standards.

Catalog evidence and verification needed
- Evidence in memory: presence of “adjustable desk lamps,” “task lamps,” and “Harbor Task Lamp” in the catalog shows candidate products exist.
- Missing/required verification: for any specific lamp (including the Harbor Task Lamp) you should verify:
  - Exact lumens, wattage, and lm/W (efficacy).
  - CRI and color temperature options.
  - Dimming capability and control type.
  - ENERGY STAR or DLC listing (if claimed).
  - Presence and behavior of occupancy sensors or smart features (if claimed).
  - Rated lifetime and warranty terms.
  - Physical adjustability, shade design (glare control), and mounting (clamp/base) to fit your desks.
  - Price and any available rebates.

Practical picks to consider from the catalog (based on entries found)
- Adjustable LED task lamp (general category) — best all-around choice for task lighting when specs meet targets above.
- Low‑profile LED desk lamp with diffuse panel — good if you want even, low‑glare illumination across the work surface.
- Harbor Task Lamp (catalog entry found) — consider as a candidate but check the detailed specs listed above; I don’t have its technical data in memory.

If you want, I can:
- Pull detailed spec sheets and compare 3–4 specific lamps from the catalog (I’ll verify lumens, watts, CRI, dimming, certifications).
- Recommend the single best lamp for your office if you tell me desk size, number of lamps needed, preferred style, and budget.
